name: Valdenoceda prison memorial
story: In an old silk factory in the Valdivielso valley north of Burgos, the Franco regime ran a prison for Republican prisoners, many transferred from other jails and from the Northern front. Cold, hunger and disease killed 153 inmates between 1938 and 1943, and they were buried in the village cemetery. The victims' association counts 154, adding a man killed at Valdenoceda in 1936 before the prison opened. From 2007 the association exhumed 114 bodies and identified many of them, making it one of the best-documented cases of prison mortality in Franco's Spain.
see: The shell of the factory-prison beside the Ebro, and the cemetery with memorial for the prisoners.
plan: Small village on the N-232 about 1 h from Burgos; building exterior only; cemetery accessible.

boxes.text: view it from the road or public path only.
